jobs.title: Director, Customer Intelligence
jobs.description:
Reporting to the VP, Advanced Analytics, the Director, Customer Intelligence will develop and execute our Customer Analytics Intake across multiple data analysis teams.

This role will establish a center of practice for how analytics requests enter the organization, establish clear priorities, and coordinate work through delivery.

The role will serve as the operating hub and delivery lead for enterprise customer and commercial analytics. It will bring structure to incoming demand, protect the capacity of specialist teams, and ensure business partners have clear visibility into scope, ownership, timelines, dependencies, and expected outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Own the end-to-end intake process for analytics, BI, measurement, and data requests from the COO and CCO organizations.
Lead a weekly intake forum, maintain a shared prioritization framework, and establish transparent service levels.
Partner with business stakeholders to clarify objectives, define requirements, assess readiness, and agree on expected outcomes.
Evaluate incoming requests and coordinate assignment to the appropriate Customer Analytics, Advanced Analytics, Measurement, or Data Engineering team.
Escalate capacity constraints, competing priorities, and delivery trade-offs requiring leadership decisions.
Establish clear rules of engagement, request templates, governance routines, and a single visible backlog.
Ensure business partners understand the status, owner, next milestone, and expected timing of each request.
Lead planning and delivery coordination
Translate approved requests into clearly defined scope, deliverables, timelines, milestones, and accountabilities.
Coordinate project activities across business, analytics, data, technology, and other enabling teams.
Maintain project plans and track progress against agreed commitments.
Monitor risks, issues, dependencies, scope changes, and decisions throughout delivery.
Facilitate working sessions, status reviews, and governance meetings to keep initiatives moving forward.
Provide clear and consistent updates to stakeholders and senior leaders.
Support the transition of completed work back into the business and confirm that agreed outcomes have been delivered.
Provide intake consulting and request support
Help business partners frame requests, define the business need, and determine the appropriate delivery path.
Distinguish between short-cycle requests and larger initiatives requiring formal planning, prioritization, and specialist support.
Develop presentations and materials that communicate project objectives, delivery status, decisions, risks, and outcomes.
Build and maintain reusable intake materials, project templates, KPI explainers, and business reference materials that improve consistency and reduce repeat requests.
Connect business, Analytics, and Data teams
Partner closely with the AVPs and Managers leading Analytics, Data, and Data Science to ensure work is scoped, prioritized, and handed off effectively.
Build strong domain knowledge across CTR, Mark’s, SportChek, Merchandising, Marketing, Customer Strategy, Digital, and Triangle.
Identify recurring requests, delivery challenges, and capability gaps through the intake process.
Feed patterns into planning and prioritization discussions to identify repeatable solutions, improved processes, or longer-term investments.
Promote consistent ways of working across business, Analytics, Data, and Technology teams.
Represent the intake and delivery function
Be the first call for senior COO and CCO leaders when they need support navigating an analytics, measurement, BI, or data request.
Provide clear guidance on request status, ownership, delivery approach, timelines, and next steps.
Present intake trends, portfolio status, delivery risks, capacity considerations, and program impact in business reviews and executive forums.
Ensure communication is concise, practical, and focused on the decisions or actions required.

What You Bring

Post-secondary education in Business, Project Management, Economics, Analytics, or a related discipline.
6+ years of experience in project management, business consulting, demand management, portfolio coordination, analytics operations, or a related role.
Demonstrated experience establishing or operating an intake, demand management, project governance, or centre of excellence function.
Strong experience defining business requirements, developing project plans, and coordinating work across multiple teams.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities, capacity constraints, delivery dependencies, and changes in scope.
Experience facilitating governance forums, prioritization discussions, working sessions, and executive updates.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate complex requests into clear scope, accountabilities, plans, and decisions.
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior business leaders and cross-functional partners.
General familiarity with analytics, BI, measurement, and data environments sufficient to support effective intake, scoping, and delivery coordination.
Project management certification or equivalent practical experience is an asset.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
Manulife is transforming how we deliver digital experiences across our businesses and markets. Through Digital Storefront, we are building a portfolio of enterprise digital capabilities that make it easier, faster and more effective for our segments to deliver differentiated, connected experiences for customers.

As Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities, you will lead a team responsible for the strategy, execution, evolution, adoption and value realization of a portfolio of enterprise common capabilities that support Manulife's digital strategy across Canada, the United States, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

This is an enterprise product leadership role. You will establish the future-state vision and value proposition for assigned capabilities, understand segment needs and roadmaps, define and continuously evolve the enterprise roadmap, determine MVP and subsequent releases, and work across business, technology, experience and delivery teams to bring capabilities to market.

Working closely with peer capability leaders, you will ensure individual capability roadmaps come together as a cohesive enterprise portfolio aligned to segment strategies and evolving customer and business needs.

You will work closely with the Common Capability Collective, which brings together segment and enterprise stakeholders to identify needs, establish priorities and align investments. You will ensure capabilities solve meaningful business and customer problems, are designed for reuse across Manulife, and continue to evolve based on adoption, performance, emerging technology and changing business needs.

Success is not simply delivering a capability. It is ensuring that capabilities are adopted, generate measurable value and become stronger over time.

Position Responsibilities

Capability Strategy & Vision

Own the strategy, future-state vision and evolution of assigned enterprise digital capabilities.
Define the business and customer problems each capability is intended to solve and articulate a compelling enterprise value proposition.
Establish clear business outcomes, benefits and success measures for each capability.
Maintain an understanding of customer expectations, industry trends, competitive practices and emerging technologies to inform capability direction.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and reuse capabilities across markets and businesses while enabling appropriate market differentiation.
Actively identify and embed opportunities to leverage AI, GenAI and agentic AI within enterprise capabilities and delivery practices to create differentiated customer experiences, accelerate delivery and improve business outcomes.

Roadmap & Product Leadership

Own and continuously evolve multi-year capability roadmaps that translate enterprise strategy into actionable priorities and investments.
Align capability roadmaps with segment strategies, product roadmaps, customer journeys and technology dependencies.
Define MVPs and subsequent releases that balance customer and business value, speed to market, enterprise scalability and technical feasibility.
Translate capability vision and business outcomes into clear requirements, priorities and measurable objectives for delivery teams.
Make informed prioritization and trade-off decisions based on customer value, business value, reuse potential, effort, dependencies and strategic alignment.
Partner with architecture, technology, data, experience, AI and delivery teams to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise scale, integration and reuse.

Common Capability Collective & Enterprise Alignment

Work with the Common Capability Collective as the primary forum for gathering segment needs, identifying common requirements, establishing priorities and aligning capability investments.
Build strong partnerships across Canada, the United States, Asia, Global Wealth & Asset Management and Global functions to understand their strategies, roadmaps and evolving capability needs.
Identify commonality across segment requirements and translate individual needs into scalable enterprise solutions where appropriate.
Facilitate decisions and trade-offs when priorities differ across markets or businesses.
Maintain transparency on capability priorities, roadmaps, dependencies, delivery progress and value realization.
Ensure segment perspectives remain represented throughout the capability lifecycle—from strategy and design through implementation and ongoing evolution.

Capability Launch, Adoption & Evolution

Lead capabilities from strategy and concept through MVP, launch, adoption and ongoing maturity.
Develop capability rollout and adoption strategies in partnership with segments and delivery teams.
Work with markets and businesses to integrate enterprise capabilities into their digital experiences and roadmaps.
Identify barriers to adoption and work across teams to resolve them.
Establish feedback loops with users, segments and stakeholders to understand how capabilities are performing in practice.
Use adoption data, customer insights, analytics and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve capabilities and identify new opportunities.
Ensure capabilities evolve as customer expectations, segment requirements, technology and enterprise strategy change.

Value Realization & Performance

Define measurable outcomes and KPIs for assigned capabilities before investment and delivery.
Establish baselines and targets that enable Manulife to understand the incremental value created through common capabilities.
Track and report capability adoption, utilization, customer outcomes, business impact, operational efficiency and other relevant measures.
Demonstrate how enterprise capabilities contribute to segment and enterprise objectives.
Use performance data and insights to identify opportunities for optimization, further investment or changes in direction.
Develop clear executive-level reporting on capability performance, value realization, roadmap progress and emerging opportunities.
Ensure investment decisions continue to be grounded in measurable customer and business value.

Team & Portfolio Leadership

Lead, coach and develop a small team of product and capability resources, providing clear direction, priorities and opportunities for growth.
Work closely with peer Directors to manage enterprise digital capabilities as an integrated portfolio, aligning strategies, roadmaps, priorities, dependencies and investment decisions across capabilities.
Identify connections and dependencies across capabilities to ensure they evolve together to enable cohesive customer and business experiences.
Share resources and expertise across the capability portfolio where appropriate, dynamically aligning capacity to the highest-value priorities.
Foster consistent product management practices, ways of working and measures of success across the Enterprise Digital Capabilities team.
Create an environment of collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement across the team.

Enterprise Leadership & Communication

Act as an enterprise advocate and subject-matter leader for assigned capabilities.
Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities and the value they can create for markets and businesses.
Communicate capability vision, strategy, roadmap and value through clear and compelling storytelling tailored to executive, business and technical audiences.
Influence across organizational boundaries and build alignment among stakeholders with different priorities.
Bring together business, experience, data and technology perspectives to drive enterprise decisions.
Champion an enterprise-first mindset while recognizing legitimate market, regulatory and customer differences.
Contribute to the broader evolution of Manulife's enterprise digital capability portfolio and Digital Storefront strategy.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience in digital product management, capability management, digital strategy, platform strategy or related disciplines, including experience operating at a senior product leadership level.
Demonstrated experience defining product or capability vision, strategy, value propositions and multi-year roadmaps.
Experience taking digital products or capabilities from concept and MVP through launch, adoption and continuous evolution.
Strong understanding of digital platforms and enterprise capabilities, with the ability to work effectively across business, technology, architecture, data and experience teams.
Demonstrated ability to translate business and customer needs into scalable solutions and actionable product priorities.
Experience defining and measuring product or capability outcomes, including adoption, customer, operational and financial metrics.
Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to use data, customer insights and performance metrics to inform decisions and identify opportunities.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching and developing talent, setting priorities and effectively deploying resources across competing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to lead through both direct accountability and influence, building alignment across teams, peers and senior stakeholders in a complex matrixed organization.
Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with experience navigating complex, matrixed organizations.
Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics and articulate business value.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across stakeholders with different priorities and requirements.
Demonstrated experience applying AI, GenAI and agentic AI to product and capability strategy, delivery and evolution—identifying and implementing opportunities to improve customer and business outcomes, accelerate delivery and increase productivity.
AI-first approach to ways of working, with demonstrated use of AI in day-to-day practices to improve analysis, research, planning, decision-making, communication and execution, and an expectation to continuously identify new opportunities to embed AI into how the team operates.
Financial services, insurance or wealth management experience is an asset.

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities will ensure Manulife's common capabilities are not simply technology investments—they are enterprise products that solve meaningful customer and business problems, are adopted across the organization and deliver measurable value.
Success means creating a clear line of sight from segment need → enterprise opportunity → capability vision → roadmap → MVP → adoption → measurable value → continuous evolution.
It also means ensuring individual capabilities do not evolve in isolation. Working with peer capability leaders, the Common Capability Collective and segment partners, the Director will help create an integrated enterprise capability portfolio in which roadmaps, investments, dependencies and resources come together to enable more connected customer experiences and accelerate delivery across Manulife.
Ultimately, the role enables Manulife to build once where it makes sense, reuse at scale, continuously improve and maximize the value of our enterprise digital investments.

When You Join Our Team

As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping people make their decisions easier and lives better. To learn more about us, visit https://www.manulife.com/en/about/our-story.html.

jobs.title: Director of Computer Vision
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Aperçu de l’entreprise

Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.

Department Overview

Motorola Solutions' innovations, products, and services play essential roles in people's lives. Our end-to-end suite of software solutions helps customers manage emergency communications, process video and evidence, and leverage cutting-edge AI-driven analytics for security and operational insights. We are industry leaders in video security and analytics, with solutions deployed in more than 120 countries across diverse environments such as school campuses, transportation systems, healthcare centers, public venues, critical infrastructure, prisons, factories, casinos, airports, financial institutions, government facilities, and retailers. Our AI-powered security solutions integrate advanced video analytics, machine learning, and embedded intelligence to enable proactive threat detection, enhanced situational awareness, and automated decision-making.

Job Description

Job DescriptionThe Director of Computer Vision will drive the technical vision, research and engineering execution for the platform, with focus on the following core areas:

Foundational Research Strategy: Define the long-term research agenda for fundamental computer vision capabilities and drive the culture of scientific excellence.
Technical Vision, Engineering Leadership, and Execution: Provide executive technical leadership to a unified research and engineering organization, defining the technical architecture, strategy, and engineering roadmap for the Computer Vision Platform. Drive execution, ensuring the seamless translation of product requirements into robust technical specifications and successful delivery of next-generation visual intelligence solutions that are highly scalable and align with overall product and business strategy.
Organizational Leadership and Talent Strategy: Manage and scale a unified computer vision research and engineering organization distributed across multiple geographies, overseeing multiple teams, and defining the strategy for recruiting, mentoring, and attracting world-class talent.
End-to-End MLOps and Deployment: Own the entire engineering lifecycle for central, reusable computer vision models and foundational AI infrastructure. This includes establishing best-in-class MLOps practices for scalable training, efficient deployment, continuous monitoring, and performance optimization across edge and cloud environments.
Performance Measurement and Continuous Improvement: Define, implement, and track key technical performance metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, model efficiency, system reliability) to measure engineering success, identify bottlenecks, and drive continuous improvement in execution and delivery.
Technical Innovation and Risk Management: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge computer vision research and technologies. Proactively identify and mitigate significant technical risks, and lead critical engineering decisions, including build-versus-buy analysis.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations, with a focus on building and deploying enterprise-scale platforms and solutions in production.
Technical Acumen & Deep Expertise: Deep, demonstrable expertise in computer vision, machine learning algorithms, and the end-to-end MLOps lifecycle, including 5+ years of hands-on experience building and optimizing computer vision models or as a computer vision researcher. Proven ability to engage in complex technical discussions, define the architectural vision for central, reusable AI infrastructure and models, and drive technical strategy while managing critical trade-offs.
Executive Technical Strategy & Metrics: Proven experience defining long-term technical vision, engineering strategy, and roadmaps for a large-scale platform. Expertise in defining and implementing technical metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, system reliability, model efficiency) to measure engineering excellence and drive continuous improvement across an organization.
Organizational & People Leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage and scale a unified, distributed engineering and research organization of 50 to 100 people, mentor senior technical talent, and lead multiple teams across different geographies.
Strong Analytical and Research Skills: Hands-on experience driving innovation through foundational research, working with AI performance metrics (e.g., Precision/Recall), real-time video processing, and inference optimization.
Customer-Driven Technical Leadership (Pathfinding): Track record of translating highly ambiguous product concepts and complex customer needs into clear, executable technical roadmaps and architectural specifications.
Start-up Mentality & Agility: Experience in a start-up or fast-paced environment is highly valued, demonstrating high ownership, bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to drive 0-to-1 product development with limited resources.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in public safety, security-focused software (e.g., video security, evidence management), mission-critical systems, or emergency communications is a plus.

Target Base Salary Range: $230,000 CAD - $270,000 CAD

Consistent with Motorola Solutions values and applicable law, we provide the following information to promote pay transparency and equity. Pay within this range varies and depends on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The actual offer will be based on the individual candidate.

Note: Candidates must reside in a Canada within the Eastern (EST) or Central (CST) Time Zone.

Basic Requirements

Bachelors degree with 10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations.

Travel Requirements

10-25%

Relocation Provided

None

Position Type

Experienced

Referral Payment Plan

No

EEO Statement

Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally-protected characteristic.

We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. If you’d like to join our team but feel that you don’t quite meet all of the preferred skills, we’d still love to hear why you think you’d be a great addition to our team.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruiting experience for candidates with disabilities, or other physical or mental health conditions. To request an accommodation, please complete this Reasonable Accommodations Form so we can assist you.

Motorola Solutions adopte, favorise et promeut les principes de diversité, d’équité et d’inclusion. Nous encourageons et accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, quelles que soient leur race, origines ethnique, religion ou croyance, orientation sexuelle, identité et expression sexuelle, statut d’anciens combattants ou tout autre statut protégé par la Loi.

jobs.title: Field Operations - Operations Director
jobs.description:
Job Profile – Operations Director

We take care of those dedicated to taking care of animals.

VetStrategy is Canada's leading veterinary network, with over 360 hospitals and clinics and more than 5,500 veterinary professionals across the country. As part of IVC Evidensia, we support veterinary teams with the resources, expertise and operational leadership they need to deliver exceptional care and build thriving practices.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Operations Director. This key leadership role is responsible for ensuring operational excellence across multiple veterinary practices, driving efficiency, and fostering a culture of accountability and high performance. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in operations management, exceptional leadership skills, and a proven track record of successfully managing multiple locations. The Operations Director works closely with Regional Medical Directors and corporate leaders to consistent delivery of best-in-class care, ensuring our practices embody and operate in alignment with VetStrategy’s values and Leadership Behaviours.

Work Location:
Hamilton/Niagara, ON. This is a regionally based role requiring regular travel across assigned veterinary practices. Flexibility to work remotely when not required on-site.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Team Management

Lead a team of Practice Managers, taking accountability for their delivery of business and people results
Build a high-performing team by driving accountability by setting clear expectations, providing regular coaching and feedback
Be an inspiring and accessible leader, building followership with practitioners and clinic colleagues across all locations
Foster a cohesive team environment through engagement activities and active change management.
Lead by example in fostering a positive work environment, encouraging collaboration and continuous improvement.
Partner with Regional Medical Directors to support communication with clinical teams on delivery of medical information.
Ensure positive resolution of escalated employee relations issues through collaboration with the People Operations Team
Maintain a strong presence within the district through frequent communication and visits.
Support the successful integration of new practices within the district through active engagement with Integrations team throughout the onboarding process.
Engage with Regional Medical Directors to ensure that new-to-network and new graduate veterinarians are integrating well and being set up for success by ensuring action plans are in place.

Drive Operational Excellence

Monitor and analyze key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify areas for improvement and create business plans to support those enhancements.
Develop and implement strategic plans to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness across assigned district.
Oversee the execution of operational initiatives to enhance patient care and client service.
Ensure consistent implementation of standard operating procedures (SOPs) within district.
Deepen capabilities of the team through best-practice sharing and coaching to embed a customer service, data driven and growth mindset

Financial Management

Oversee the creation and management of district practice budgets, ensuring financial targets are met.
Analyze district financial performance, drawing insight and taking action in response to trends.
Work with marketing teams to drive client acquisition and retention.
Ensure cost-effectiveness with resources and operational processes while maintaining high service standards and financial health.
Investment in practices: Identify and support the execution of investments in refurbishments, facilities, equipment, and technology so that practices provide the best possible care for patients.

Strategic Initiatives

Lead and collaborate on cross-functional projects to develop and implement strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing the financial performance of the business.
Lead the implementation of strategic initiatives and ensure alignment with the organization's goals and objectives within the district.
Communicate corporate policies and procedures to Practice Managers, ensuring understanding and compliance.
Monitor the effectiveness of corporate initiatives and provide feedback for continuous improvement.
Identify opportunities for business growth, including new services and marketing initiatives.

Compliance and Safety

Ensure all practices comply with relevant regulations, standards, and safety protocols.
Partner with Regional Medical Directors respond to adverse events, ensuring reporting and appropriate action are taken in response.
Include Regional Medical Directors in regular district meetings with Practice Managers to review and discuss clinical compliance and safety, updates to provincial regulations.
Review and evaluate Continuing Education (“CE”) approval decisions made by Practice Managers, ensuring practice teams are focused on learning that contributes to personal growth while elevating our practice.

Marketing & Client Relations

Lead the evaluation of local market assessments and promotions to identify opportunities for growth.
Work closely with the Marketing team to develop targeted marketing strategies based on local market assessments.
Ensure the successful execution of network-wide promotions, aligning them with local needs and preferences.
Collaborate with the national marketing team to exchange ideas and initiatives, fostering a cohesive marketing approach
Resolve escalated client relations issues to a positive end, engaging the Regional Medical Director where required.

Key Qualifications

Leadership Experience: Minimum of 7 years of experience in a management role, preferably in human or veterinary healthcare.
Education: Bachelor's degree in business administration, healthcare management, or a related field preferred.
Financial Acumen: Thorough understanding of financial management, including budgeting and financial reporting.
Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting formal business plans.
Organizational Skills: Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Conflict Resolution: Demonstrated ability to effectively resolve conflicts within a team, utilizing strong interpersonal and communication skills to mediate disputes and foster a collaborative work environment
Client-Focused: A commitment to providing high-quality customer service and improving the overall client experience.
Critical Thinking: Proven ability to analyze complex situations, identify key issues, and develop effective solutions. Demonstrates strong problem-solving skills and the capacity to make well-informed decisions under pressure.
IT Proficiency: Comfortable with Microsoft Office, and other digital tools for managing administrative tasks.

jobs.title: Business Development Vice President
jobs.description:
Position Description

The Vice President of Business Development is responsible for growing CGI’s business with one of Canada’s large banks in Toronto. Embedded within the client’s financial services environment, this management role leads a team of more than 60 CGI Partners and brings together client relationship leadership, business development, engagement oversight, and operational performance.

The successful candidate brings a strong background in solutions-led IT consulting and can connect the client’s business priorities with practical technology and consulting solutions. They understand the Canadian banking sector and can guide opportunities from discovery and solution shaping through proposal and delivery. Areas of focus may include digital and technology modernization, data and AI, cybersecurity and resilience, risk, regulatory change, and operational transformation.

Work location: This role requires a minimum of five days per week at the client’s downtown Toronto office and/or CGI’s downtown Toronto office. This requirement may change at any time.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Engagement and Mission Governance

Oversee the successful delivery of client engagements and the evolution of end-to-end service offerings.
Coordinate and monitor the quality of services delivered to clients.
Apply the CGI Project Management Framework (CPMF), including conducting regular reviews of project and operational performance with CGI Partners and clients.
Collaborate with internal CGI partners to deliver integrated, end-to-end services to clients.

Client Relationships and Business Development

Own and strengthen relationships with assigned clients.
Build and maintain relationships with existing and prospective clients.
Lead and manage business development activities.

Team and Partner Leadership

Oversee the assignment, recruitment, and career development of team members.
Develop the team’s capabilities and expertise to meet client needs and respond to market changes.
Support the health and well-being of CGI Partners.

Business and Operations Management

Lead the team to achieve budget, revenue, and profitability targets.
Contribute to strategic and operational planning.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

Significant experience in solutions-led IT consulting, developing technology and consulting solutions around clients’ business needs.
strong track record of growing strategic client accounts and leading business development in the financial services sector.
Experience working with large Canadian banks, with an understanding of their business priorities, operating environments, and risk, security, and regulatory considerations.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior business and technology executives and influence decisions across complex organizations.
Experience leading consultative sales and pursuits, from opportunity identification and solution shaping through proposal development, negotiation, and handoff to delivery.
Strong financial and operational management skills, including accountability for revenue, budgets, and profitability.
Experience leading and developing large consulting teams, including workforce planning, recruitment, career development, and performance management.
A record of overseeing complex client engagements and maintaining strong service quality, governance, and client outcomes.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

At CGI, we value the strength that diversity brings and are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone belongs. The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.

Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.

Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Leadership team through the Customer Services and Informatics division to execute a full range of department-wide services to meet targets and objectives of the Strategic Plan. This includes supporting and developing business plans; ensuring consistent and effective implementation; enhancing integration; standardizing services and business practices; maximizing efficiencies and cost savings.
Responsible for business transformational projects through assessment, analysis, design and implementation; champions the implementation of change management initiatives, process and execution.
Leads the development of a Monitoring Framework with key performance indicators for each unit within the department and develops remedial and continuous improvement plans in relation to results. This framework includes leading and lagging indicators and an effective client satisfaction monitoring and reporting system to evaluate the services provided by the entire Facilities group.
Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

Failure to ensure alignment and direction for Facilities in this role will negatively impact on the reputation of the University. The consequence of poor decisions have human resources, legal and representational consequences and in addition to costs. Failure to effectively direct major projects that transform business operations through change or to ensure accurate asset information for facilities planning, major capital decisions, or maintenance, construction and renovation activities will lead to the loss of millions of dollars in investment, inefficiencies or unrealized efficiency benefits, and potential safety issues.

Supervision Received

Works autonomously within broad objectives under the senior administrative direction of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Supervision Given

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics manages a workforce of approximately 35 employees. The Director is directly responsible for supervising work of 6 professional staff in manager and senior manager roles, with a diverse portfolio of supporting units including the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This position will also act as the Associate Vice-President, Facilities from time to time.

Undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline. Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Minimum of 9 years of related experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion

Preferred Qualifications

Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Master of Business Administration or equivalent preferred. 12 years experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience in transforming businesses within complex unionized environments preferred.
Significant experience in areas of strategic planning, tactical planning, change management, project management, risk management, information system management, business process improvement, critical and systems thinking, continuous improvement, quality assurance, adult education and maintenance, operations management and organizational design would be advantageous.

•        Track budget to actual, forecast cash flow, and flag variances early

•        Build and maintain budgets for programs, capital projects, and new initiatives

Funding and compliance

•        Manage financial reporting under Indigenous Services Canada agreements and other federal, provincial, and third-party funding

•        Make sure the Nation meets its obligations under funding agreements, contracts, and applicable legislation

•        Prepare for and respond to funder reviews and audits

Governance, policy, and controls

•        Maintain and update financial policies, procedures, and internal controls, including any Financial Administration Law requirements

•        Support Finance and Audit processes and provide clear financial information to Chief and Council

•        Review contracts, agreements, and joint ventures for financial impact

Own-source revenue and economic development

•        Support financial oversight of Nation-owned businesses, partnerships, and joint ventures

•        Provide financial analysis for new business and land-based opportunities

Team leadership

•        Supervise and develop finance staff

•        Work closely with Operations, Lands, Human Resources, and program staff

Taxes and statutory filings

•        Oversee CRA remittances and other statutory requirements

Qualifications Required

•        CPA designation (CPA, CGA, CMA, or CA) or CAFM

•        5 or more years of progressive financial management experience, including at least 2 years supervising staff

•        Strong knowledge of budgeting, financial statements, audit processes, and internal controls

•        Experience with accounting software and advanced Excel skills

•        Strong written and verbal communication

•        Valid BC driver's licence and a clear criminal record check (required for the role)

Preferred

•        Experience in a First Nation, Indigenous organization, non-profit, or public sector setting

•        Familiarity with ISC funding agreements and First Nation financial reporting

at the start of employment to learn the financial structure, meet the community, and work closely with the organization. After successful completion of the probationary period, the Nation will review a hybrid arrangement
(for example, up to 2 days per week remote), based on performance and operational needs. Some in-person attendance will always be required, including Council meetings, audit, and community events.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Leadership team through the Customer Services and Informatics division to execute a full range of department-wide services to meet targets and objectives of the Strategic Plan. This includes supporting and developing business plans; ensuring consistent and effective implementation; enhancing integration; standardizing services and business practices; maximizing efficiencies and cost savings.
Responsible for business transformational projects through assessment, analysis, design and implementation; champions the implementation of change management initiatives, process and execution.
Leads the development of a Monitoring Framework with key performance indicators for each unit within the department and develops remedial and continuous improvement plans in relation to results. This framework includes leading and lagging indicators and an effective client satisfaction monitoring and reporting system to evaluate the services provided by the entire Facilities group.
Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

Failure to ensure alignment and direction for Facilities in this role will negatively impact on the reputation of the University. The consequence of poor decisions have human resources, legal and representational consequences and in addition to costs. Failure to effectively direct major projects that transform business operations through change or to ensure accurate asset information for facilities planning, major capital decisions, or maintenance, construction and renovation activities will lead to the loss of millions of dollars in investment, inefficiencies or unrealized efficiency benefits, and potential safety issues.

Supervision Received

Works autonomously within broad objectives under the senior administrative direction of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Supervision Given

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics manages a workforce of approximately 35 employees. The Director is directly responsible for supervising work of 6 professional staff in manager and senior manager roles, with a diverse portfolio of supporting units including the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This position will also act as the Associate Vice-President, Facilities from time to time.

Minimum Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline. Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Minimum of 9 years of related experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion

Preferred Qualifications

Eligibility for membership in a professional Institute or Association. Master of Business Administration or equivalent preferred. 12 years experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience in transforming businesses within complex unionized environments preferred.
Significant experience in areas of strategic planning, tactical planning, change management, project management, risk management, information system management, business process improvement, critical and systems thinking, continuous improvement, quality assurance, adult education and maintenance, operations management and organizational design would be advantageous.
Formal education in Project Management and/or a Project Management Professional (PMP) designation or another relevant discipline is an asset. Proven ability to initiate, plan and execute business projects.
Experience working in a complex, multi-departmental organization.
Experienced in leadership development, facilitation, coaching and mentoring.
Significant experience in leading large-scale transformation and change initiatives within complex, multi-union environments.
Strong leadership skills with emphasis on decision-making, problem solving, consulting, marketing, facilitation, negotiation and team-building skills and the ability to foster a motivating and respectful work environment.
Strong interpersonal and oral and written communication skills, emphasizing listening, and negotiating; bargaining, compromising, and conciliation; ability to summarize needs, determine priorities and necessities
Demonstrated leadership and organizational abilities; mature judgment, ability to make decisions under time constraints, managing risk and uncertainty, multi-tasking, and ability to set priorities.
